title: Payments slow right after release
executive_summary: The payment-service 5.8.0 release (11:32Z) is unlikely to be the cause. Errors and DB connection pressure in payment-service began at 11:28Z, and the earliest anomaly is in postgres (p99 latency onset 11:23Z, after storage write-latency warnings on volume vol-0a3f from 11:21Z). The most likely cause is degraded storage on the Postgres volume vol-0a3f, slowing writes and checkpoints, which pushed charges.insert past its 2000ms statement timeout and held payment DB connections. Long-running report_rollup() queries are a likely contributor. Order-service latency and error rate were flat, so the reported order-service degradation is not supported by telemetry.

hypotheses.description: Degraded block storage volume vol-0a3f on the Postgres host slowed WAL/checkpoint writes, causing charges.insert statement timeouts in payment-service and DB connection saturation. Mechanism: Storage write latency rose (835ms avg at 11:21Z) -> WAL writes and checkpoints slow (checkpoint took 453s) -> Postgres p99 latency rises from 11:23Z -> payment charges.insert exceeds 2000ms statement_timeout (from 11:28Z) -> payment DB connection utilisation climbs to ~80% -> payment errors rise to ~9%.

probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): infrastructure_degradation in postgres - Degraded block storage volume vol-0a3f on the Postgres host slowed WAL/checkpoint writes, causing charges.insert statement timeouts in payment-service and DB connection saturation.
corrective_actions: Mitigate the storage issue: fail over Postgres to a replica or migrate off vol-0a3f, and confirm with the cloud provider.
Pause or reschedule report_rollup() during incident recovery.
Do not roll back 5.8.0 on current evidence; revisit only if per-version error data shows it contributes.
preventive_actions: Alert on Postgres storage write latency and checkpoint duration.
Isolate reporting queries onto a replica or a separate resource pool.
Add per-version error breakdowns to release monitoring so deploy attribution is unambiguous.
monitoring_recommendations: Track vol-0a3f write latency and disk IO wait with a threshold alert.
Monitor Postgres checkpoint duration and WAL write time.
Alert on charges.insert statement timeout counts in payment-service.
Collect disk_io_wait_ms for postgres and payment-service.
limitations: Timing-based correlation analysis; no direct causal test.
Telemetry limited to the window provided.
[agent-reported gap] No disk_io_wait_ms for postgres; no IOPS or cloud health data for vol-0a3f.
[agent-reported gap] No pg_stat_activity or lock data.
[agent-reported gap] Payment p99 latency flat despite DB timeouts; not explained.
[agent-reported gap] Order-service degradation reported by the team is not visible in its metrics.
[agent-reported gap] No scheduler record for report_rollup().
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The release 5.8.0 is not supported as the cause. The earliest anomaly is Postgres storage and write degradation (volume vol-0a3f, from 11:21Z), which precedes the payment errors (11:28Z) and the deploy (11:32Z). That degradation most likely caused charges.insert statement timeouts and connection saturation in payment-service. The report_rollup() workload is a plausible contributor. Confidence is moderate because host-level IO data for Postgres was not collected and the flat payment p99 is unexplained.
